=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1878-1886; .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:421-429; .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4889-4897 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The newly added FAIL-line annotation emitter duplicates the existing #6885 emitter, causing duplicate annotations and breaking the existing per-shard cap and truncation behavior.
  WHY: The existing block already emits FAIL-line annotations, so both emitters run for each failed shard and CI tests fail with excess annotations.
- tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py:843-869 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The new annotation tests assume their mechanism is the only source of matching annotations, so their expected counts fail when the existing #6885 loop also emits them.
  WHY: The test assertions expect exactly 5 annotations and exactly 1 truncated-line annotation, but the existing loop adds matching annotations.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1879; .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:422; .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4890 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The no-FAIL fallback uses the `::error::orchestrate-poll shard N: ` prefix reserved for real FAIL lines.
  WHY: `test_fail_lines_must_start_with_the_runner_prefix` forbids that prefix when no runner FAIL line exists, and the new fallback violates the test.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1879-1883; .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:422-426; .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4890-4894 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The fallback labels any failed shard without a FAIL line as a “runner or fixture error,” which mischaracterizes cases such as an OOM kill or timeout.
  WHY: The label can mislead triage about the cause; Sonnet rates this BLOCKER while Gemini rates it MAJOR.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1881 and 1905-1908; .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:424 and 433-436; .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4892 and 4901-4903 | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The plain-text failure list is built from workflow-command-escaped lines, so it prints escape sequences such as `%25` and `%0D` instead of the raw failure text.
  WHY: The output is garbled for triage, and the list is an additional copy of lines already emitted or summarized.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1878; .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:421; .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:4889 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new code reuses `shard_fail_lines`, which the existing #6885 block already creates as an array, as a scalar name.
  WHY: The scalar assignment collides with the existing array identifier; although no immediate failure is reported, it leaves stale array elements and violates identifier uniqueness.
- changelog.d/6883-orchestrate-poll-fail-annotations.md:3-12 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The changelog claims an annotation cap of 5 per step and describes a fallback that do not match the shipped behavior, and repeats claims already present in other changelog fragments.
  WHY: The existing #6885 loop already emits up to 20 FAIL-line annotations per shard, making the documented cap and “plain-text list holds the rest” claim inaccurate.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1878 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The 500-character cut is applied before percent escaping, so percent-heavy FAIL lines can exceed 500 rendered characters.
  WHY: Escaping `%` to `%25` can increase the rendered line length by up to 1.5 times, so the stated bound does not hold for all input.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The changelog fragment describes behavior the merged code does not have, including “Test-name annotations per step | at most 5 (the plain-text list holds the rest)” and “Exit codes and the existing error lines are unchanged”.
  expected_change_site: changelog.d/6883-orchestrate-poll-fail-annotations.md
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: lines 1-17 describe an annotation cap of 5 and a plain-text list, while the existing #6885 loop already emits up to 20 annotations per shard.
- requirement: "Make failed shards report their failing test names and errors in CI annotations and the job log, with a fallback when no failure line exists." (AD-2 and the AI issue summary).
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/ci.yml, mark-stable.yml and test-and-mark-stable.yml shard-judgment loops.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: Not absent. The #6885, #6889 and #6946 changes already deliver this in all three workflows. The only net effect of the added block is the duplication above. The correct delivery is to drop the duplicated emitter and keep only whatever the existing loop lacks (the 500-character truncation, if wanted), updating the tests and the changelog to match.
- requirement: Issue #6883 and AD-1/AD-3 ask for a local reproduction of the module failure, a fix only if one is confirmed, and no weakening of checks.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py or scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, only if a defect reproduces on `main`.
  confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: The PR changes neither file. The earlier autofix comment attributes shard 1's original failure (`test_security_pass_cap_converts_low_keep_fixing_to_advisory`) to a branch that was behind `main`. The current merge commit 39583d2 carries `main`'s changes, and the failures in the latest CI run all come from the new `ShardFailAnnotationTest` and `ShardJudgeTest` cases, not from a poller test. This is therefore not a gap, because the PR does not need to touch those files.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
